scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls outside the standard 30-day refund window policy.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Jin Chen and I'm 80. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Hello Mr. Chen, I understand you're looking for a refund outside of our standard window. To assist you, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with the service?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and my email is jinchen@email.com.
Thank you for that. And just to confirm, could you please verify your date of birth for our security records?

Thanks. I see the account here. Per our Terms of Service, Section 4.2, refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the charge date. Since you are at 34 days, I'm not technically supposed to process this, but I can see you've been a loyal customer for years. Let me check if I can push this through.
I would really appreciate that. It was an honest mistake while I was away.

I've gone ahead and submitted an exception request for your refund. It has been approved by the system. You should see the credit of $49.99 back to your original payment method within 3-5 business days.

resolution_summary: The agent verified the customer's identity, acknowledged the policy violation, and successfully processed a one-time courtesy refund exception.
